texts.preamble: Thiru Neelagandan vs The Inspector Of Police on 11 January, 2016 Author: S.Vaidyanathan Bench: S.Vaidyanathan Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated: 11.01.2016 Coram The Hon'Ble Mr.Justice S.Vaidyanathan Crl.O.P.(MD) No.22175 of 2015 Thiru Neelagandan ... Petitioner -Vs- 1. The Inspector of Police, Aranthangi Police Station, Aranthangi. 2. Pulisingam ... Respondents Prayer: Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, to direct the 1st respondent to grant police protection to the petitioner and his land in S.No.81/14 of Koothangudi Village, Aranthangi Taluk, based on the representation dated 03.11.2015. ! For Petitioner : Mr.R.Murali ^For R1 : Mr.A.P.Balasubramani Govt. Advocate (Crl.Side) For R2 : Mr.M.Suresh :Order
texts.facts: The petitioner has come forward with this petition to direct the 1st respondent to grant police protection to the petitioner and his land in S.No.81/14 of Koothangudi Village, Aranthangi Taluk, based on the representation dated 03.11.2015. 2. The case of the petitioner is that he is the absolute owner of the land admeasuring 1 acre and 53 cents in S.No.81/14 of Koothangudi Village, Aranthangi Taluk, in which he undertakes cultivation and has made a small hut using Asbestos sheet for both residential and agricultural purposes. The Thiru Neelagandan vs The Inspector Of Police on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141829776/ 1 petitioner is also the patta holder of the said land. It is submitted that one Pulisingam @ Prabakaran along with his henchmen, with an ulterior motive to usurp the property, threatened the petitioner to leave the village. When the petitioner lodged a complaint with the Police, they advised him to approach the competent civil forum. 2.1. It is also submitted that thereafter, the petitioner filed a suit in O.S.No.302 of 2014 before the Sub Court, Pudukottai and the said Court was pleased to grant interim injunction in I.A.No.665 of 2014. Inspite of such order, the said Pulisingam @ Prabakaran has been repeatedly attempting to take possession of the land, as he is politically influential person. It is stated that due to the constant threat, the petitioner has given various complaints / representation for providing police protection to the petitioner and his land and since there was no response on the same, he is before this Court seeking the above relief. 5. To controvert the same, the 2nd respondent has produced a copy of the ration card, wherein the name of the 2nd respondent is shown as Puliprabakaran along with the name of the petitioner. In addition to that, he also produced a copy of his SSLC marks sheet.
texts.arguments: 3. The 2nd respondent has contested the matter by filing a counter, wherein it has been stated that he is the younger brother of the petitioner and his name is Puliprabakaran and not Pulisingam @ Prabhakaran. The petitioner is not at all in possession of the disputed site, as he is living in Chennai, doing hotel business. It is further stated that the petitioner filed the said suit as against one Pulisingam for injunction in respect of the property of the 2nd respondent, by simply referring the defendant as Pulisingam and obtained interim injunction, on the strength of which, he filed the present petition, seeking police protection, by stating the name of the 2nd respondent as Pulisingam @ Prabakaran. Thus, he played a fraud upon this Court and the same has to be looked into seriously and as the Civil Court has seized up the matter, the petitioner can very well seek such relief before the said Court. It is the stand of the 2nd respondent that he is running a water business in the name and style of ?Sakthi Agua Farm? in the disputed site and the licence was also issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 till 01.09.2016. All these material facts were suppressed by the petitioner and he has not come to the Court with clean hands. 4. In reply, the petitioner would submit that there is no Puliprabhakaran and it is only Pulisingam @ Prabhakaran, who is the younger brother of the petitioner. Therefore, it is represented by the 2nd respondent that the petitioner, in order to usurp the property, has shown his name as Pulisingam instead of Puliprabakaran in the Civil Court and committed wilfull fraud on the Court. It is no doubt true that the person, who has the benefit of judgment and decree is entitled to Police protection as per the earlier orders of this Court in the case of Radhika Sri Hari and another vs. The Commissioner of Police and another, reported in 2014-2-L.W.927 and also S.Ashokan vs. State Rep. by the Commissioner of Police and others, reported in 2015 (3) CTC 807. 9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of S.P.Chengalvaraya Naidu vs. Jagannath, reported in (1994) 1 SCC 1, has observed as under: "The courts of law are meant for imparting justice between the parties. One who comes to the court, must come with clean hands. We are constrained to say that more often than not, process of the Court is being abused. Property grabbers, tax evaders, Bank loan dodgers, and other unscrupulous persons from all walks of life find the court process a convenient lever to retain the illegal-gains indefinitely.
